title: Building Alice’s Brain: an AI Sales Rep that Learns Like a Human - Sherwood & Satwik, 11x
talk_summary: 11x describes rebuilding their AI SDR's seller knowledge base as a RAG pipeline: vendor parsing (LlamaParse, Firecrawl, Cloudglue) to markdown, header/sentence/token waterfall chunking, Pinecone storage, and a Leta-based deep-research retrieval agent, plus a 3D vector visualization for trust. The transferable lessons are mostly process: buy parsing instead of building it, ship to production before benchmarking, and lean on vendors.

takeaways.what_they_do: Split documents on markdown headers first, then sentences, then tokens, so chunks stay semantically coherent and bounded in token count rather than fixed-size token windows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we split our markdown headers and then we split on sentences and then eventually we split on tokens

takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluated parsing vendors against explicit requirements (resource types, markdown output, webhooks) and outsourced PDF/site/video-to-markdown conversion rather than building per-format parsers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we didn't want to build this from scratch ... we wanted to get to market quickly

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately deferred accuracy/comprehensiveness benchmarking and cost optimization until real production usage existed, then planned to iterate against measured baselines.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should first get to production before benchmarking and then you can improve

takeaways.technique: Deep-research retrieval agent for context gathering
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one-shot retrieval, they pass the query to an agent that plans one or many retrieval steps, executes tool calls, summarizes, and answers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it basically comes up with a plan. plan contains one or many context retrieval steps

takeaways.what_they_do: They made vendors teach them the tradeoffs (Pinecone calls on graph vs vector, LlamaParse Slack support) to shortcut their own technology evaluation.
